cost.basis: Operator's own published standard usage tariff: USD 0.05 per 1M INPUT tokens with no output billing. Two vendor sources, both snapshotted: the pricing section of https://subq.ai/ read on 14 Oct 2026 08:10Z ('In $0.05 per 1M tokens Input / Out Free Output') and the vendor's own launch post 'Introducing SubQ Snap' ('SubQ Snap is priced at $0.05 per million input tokens, with no charge for output tokens'), which also dates the tariff to the product's launch; Subquadratic's Alexander Whedon separately confirmed the figure in writing to Florian on 14 Oct 2026 01:16 Berlin (board #19133). Counted under interpretation I-1 (a manufacturer's standard, non-promotional launch list price counts from day 1 - the reading that already admitted kushal-gemma4-31b-it-autoloops). DISCLOSED: Snap is in a capacity-limited public preview - first come, first served, with a waitlist once capacity is reached - so this is the vendor's stated usage price for a product that is not yet openly bookable by everyone; CoS deputy decision #19174 rules explicitly that I-1 covers this tariff during that public preview, on the condition that the capacity limit and waitlist are stated here, as they are. The same pricing section offers 'Free 100M tokens for the first 10,000 users': that is a promotional trial credit and is deliberately NOT used - a free tier is priced at the published paid tariff, never as cost 0. The tariff is multiplied by this row's OWN measured input tokens (1,943,705 over 1,500 answered rows, mean 1,296) and divided by the full 1,500-row basis the scorer uses. The output term is zero twice over: the tariff bills no output, and the vendor's own usage meter reports 0 output tokens on all 1,500 rows. OVER THE OFFICIAL COST CAP, DISCLOSED: USD 0.064790 per 1,000 decisions is 1.003x the official cap USD 0.064595; the row is ranked (v1.6.16 vllm-sr-d3 precedent) and falls outside the official-caps board views by construction.
